# TeslaUSB Enhanced v2.1.0

Version 2.1 improves storage recovery, archive connectivity checks, and sharing
diagnostics while preserving the modern six-camera interface and Classic UI.

## Changes

- **Safer snapshot retention:** keep the newest completed snapshot when space
  is low, prefer eligible incomplete copies for cleanup, and preserve encrypted
  or uninspectable recordings. Empty or invalid completion markers cannot
  replace the last verified completed copy.
- **Verified deletion boundaries:** refuse snapshot release until successful
  mount and loop-device inspections establish that the copy is no longer in
  use. Failed, malformed, or overflowing free-space measurements stop rotation.
- **Archive destination checks:** rclone tests its configured remote destination
  with bounded requests and retry delays, replacing the unrelated one-second
  Internet ping. Transient failures do not immediately imply vehicle departure.
- **Prepare diagnostics for sharing:** review and edit a redacted copy before
  downloading it. The full local report remains available. Processing is
  bounded, truncation is shown, and the downloaded text matches the preview.
  Redaction is best effort; review the text before sharing it. Nothing is
  uploaded by this feature.
- **Development tools:** allow focused formatting of modern UI source and keep
  `tools/modern-install.py` as the stable compatibility installer entry point.

See [archive and diagnostic changes](https://github.com/jakubgt/teslausb-enhanced/pull/19)
and [snapshot safeguards](https://github.com/jakubgt/teslausb-enhanced/pull/20).

## Verification

The release source must pass the full Linux Validate workflow, including shell,
Python, JavaScript, archive integration, security-boundary, snapshot-retention,
and Chromium browser regressions. The image workflow independently checks the
embedded source, boot configuration, locked account, absence of device
credentials, package manifest, compressed stream, and uploaded asset digests.

The runtime changes were tested on an existing Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W installation:
fresh footage from all six cameras produced approximately 60-second videos,
frames decoded successfully at the start and midpoint, a new snapshot completed,
and the car's USB connection and recorder service remained healthy. A downloaded
diagnostic-sharing file matched the exact reviewed preview.

These installed-runtime checks do not establish fresh-card acceptance of a
rebuilt image. Fresh-card hardware acceptance has not been independently
confirmed. This release does not recover missing video data in already damaged
recordings or automatically delete retained recovery images.

## Image and installation

The image targets **Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W**, 64-bit Raspberry Pi OS Lite
(Debian Trixie, arm64). Download the matching `.img.xz`, `.img.xz.sha256`,
`.image-metadata.json`, and `.packages.tsv` assets from this release. Verify the
compressed image's SHA-256 before flashing. Use Raspberry Pi Imager's **Use
custom** option and the included offline configuration wizard.

Back up configuration, keys, and recordings before replacing an existing card.
Publishing this release does not automatically update an installed Pi. Recovery
images and incomplete snapshots can retain unique footage and need a separate
storage review; do not remove them indiscriminately to free space.

Existing tags and image assets remain unchanged. Do not rename an older image
to this version: each image has its own source commit, package record, and hashes.
